item.title: Correction · Pier 70 Parcel A: The 2026-10-06 entry for this record said the 2042 date comes from…
item.description: The 2026-10-06 entry for this record said the 2042 date comes from the Development Agreement's Schedule of Performance. That was wrong. The Port's 2017 staff report (Item 9B, p.7) puts the Schedule of Performance in the Disposition and Development Agreement (DDA) between the Port and the developer, which is a different agreement from the Development Agreement between the City and the developer. The report says the developer must complete phase 3 within approximately 25 years of project approval, but it never states the year 2042; 2042 is Pier & Point's own arithmetic (2017 plus 25 years). It stays labelled a legal outside date, not an expected completion. Source: https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/Item%209B%20Pier%2070%20Approval%20092217.pdf.

item.title: Correction · Pier 70 Parcel A: The 2026-09-29 entry for this record said the Brookfield…
item.description: The 2026-09-29 entry for this record said the Brookfield construction halt could only be dated to 2022, because neither source gives the month. That left out what Bisnow reports: its October 20, 2022 article says 'progress stalled in April', after 'a work stoppage earlier this year', so the halt is dated April 2022 (the year follows from 'earlier this year' in an October 2022 article). Bisnow is describing the 28-acre Pier 70 project's first phase as a whole, not this parcel in particular. The Real Deal's April 17, 2023 article says only that the developer halted construction 'last year'. The milestone stays marked approximate. Source: Bisnow, 2022-10-20 (https://www.bisnow.com/san-francisco/news/mixed-use/brookfield-properties-and-port-of-san-francisco-inch-closer-to-pier-70-completion-115959); The Real Deal, 2023-04-17 (https://therealdeal.com/san-francisco/2023/04/17/brookfield-leases-first-seven-tenants-at-pier-70/).

item.title: Correction · Pier 70 Parcel A: The 2042 date shown for Parcel A is not a deadline for this parcel…
item.description: The 2042 date shown for Parcel A is not a deadline for this parcel, which is in Phase 1; it is Pier & Point's arithmetic for the whole project's final-phase outside date in the Disposition and Development Agreement (DDA)'s Schedule of Performance, which is separate from the City's Development Agreement. The Port's report gives only years after Project approval. The date remains labelled a legal outside date, not a forecast. Source: Port of San Francisco, Item 9B: Pier 70 Mixed-Use Project approvals, Sep 22, 2017 (https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/Item%209B%20Pier%2070%20Approval%20092217.pdf); Port of San Francisco, Item 11A: Pier 70 28-Acre Site Project update, Aug 7, 2026 (https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/2026-08/item_11a_p70_project_update_-_term_sheet_overview_-_information.pdf).

item.title: Correction · Pier 70 Parcel A: The 2042 date on this record was drawn as an expected completion
item.description: The 2042 date on this record was drawn as an expected completion. The Port's 2017 staff report calls it an outside date in the Development Agreement's Schedule of Performance (Phase 3 within approximately 25 years of approval), not a construction schedule. It is now labelled a legal deadline and no longer moves this record's status on the map or the timeline. Source: https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/Item%209B%20Pier%2070%20Approval%20092217.pdf.

item.title: Correction · Pier 70 Parcel A: The Phase 1 schedule is now described as tolled by the down market…
item.description: The Phase 1 schedule is now described as tolled by the down market delay (extended to December 26, 2026, Port Item 11A) rather than lapsed, with the 2042 whole-project date kept as a soft, superseded outside date. The King Street announcement is dated Feb 22, 2023 (Bisnow's 'on Wednesday'); the October 2021 design entry says the article date is not a filing date; the July 2026 Real Deal quote was removed as a Parcel A milestone because it does not name a parcel; the unsupported 2019 mass-timber design and 365,000 GSF figure were dropped from the map notes; and claims that no Assessor lot exists were replaced with what the sources show. The board vote on the Development Agreement now shows first reading on Oct 31 and final passage on Nov 14, 2017; the Aug 11, 2026 Port Commission minutes now back the informational hearing; and the Brookfield construction halt is dated 2022 (approximate) rather than April 2022, since neither source gives the month. Source: Port of San Francisco, Commission Item 11A staff report, 2026-08-07 (https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/2026-08/item_11a_p70_project_update_-_term_sheet_overview_-_information.pdf); Port of San Francisco, Commission Item 9B staff report, 2017-09-22 (https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/Item%209B%20Pier%2070%20Approval%20092217.pdf); Bisnow, 2023-02-23 (https://www.bisnow.com/san-francisco/news/life-sciences/life-sciences-specialist-king-street-announced-plans-for-pier-70-project-117814); San Francisco Board of Supervisors, Ordinance No. 224-17 (https://sfbos.org/sites/default/files/o0224-17.pdf); Port of San Francisco, Port Commission minutes, 2026-08-11 (https://www.sfport.com/media/11558/download?inline); The Real Deal, 2026-07-16 (https://therealdeal.com/san-francisco/2026/07/16/brookfield-wants-more-apartments-at-pier-70-project/) (does not state this).
item.source: Port of San Francisco, Commission Item 11A staff report, 2026-08-07 (https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/2026-08/item_11a_p70_project_update_-_term_sheet_overview_-_information.pdf); Port of San Francisco, Commission Item 9B staff report, 2017-09-22 (https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/Item%209B%20Pier%2070%20Approval%20092217.pdf); Bisnow, 2023-02-23 (https://www.bisnow.com/san-francisco/news/life-sciences/life-sciences-specialist-king-street-announced-plans-for-pier-70-project-117814); San Francisco Board of Supervisors, Ordinance No. 224-17 (https://sfbos.org/sites/default/files/o0224-17.pdf); Port of San Francisco, Port Commission minutes, 2026-08-11 (https://www.sfport.com/media/11558/download?inline); The Real Deal, 2026-07-16 (https://therealdeal.com/san-francisco/2026/07/16/brookfield-wants-more-apartments-at-pier-70-project/) (does not state this)

item.title: Milestone · Pier 70 Parcel A: Port Commission hears an informational report (staff… (Aug 11, 2026)
item.description: Port Commission hears an informational report (staff report dated Aug 7; no action taken) on proposed DDA amendments: parcel-specific outside dates, a Project-wide affordable rate of no less than 20% (327 stand-alone affordable units kept), 65-to-90 ft height increases on certain residential parcels, developer return cut from 18% to 14%, and a new phasing plan (Aug 11, 2026). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-07; Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-11; Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-11.
item.source: Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-07; Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-11; Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-11

item.title: Planned · Pier 70 Parcel A: Port reports that although Phase 1 horizontal… (Aug 7, 2026)
item.description: Port reports that although Phase 1 horizontal infrastructure and Building 12's rehabilitation are complete, construction of Phase 1 vertical buildings and parks 'has not moved forward' because of pandemic-driven office-vacancy increases, 20-30% construction-cost escalation and higher financing costs (Aug 7, 2026). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-07.

item.title: Expected · Pier 70 Parcel A: Port Commission: Port staff and the developer are… (~Dec 2026)
item.description: Port Commission: Port staff and the developer are drafting amendments to the DDA and related transaction documents "for consideration by the Port Commission and Board of Supervisors by the end of this year or early next year" (Item 11A, memo of Aug 7, 2026, p.2 and p.6). The source gives no hearing date. The date shown is the early end of that window (December 2026); "early next year" falls in 2027. The same report proposes extending the term of the DDA, Development Agreement and Master Lease by 5 years. (~Dec 2026). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-07.

item.title: Expected · Pier 70 Parcel A: Then the Board of Supervisors: the same amendments are to… (~Dec 2026)
item.description: Then the Board of Supervisors: the same amendments are to go to the Board of Supervisors in the same window (Item 11A, p.6: "for consideration by the Port Commission and Board of Supervisors by the end of this year or early next year"). The source gives no separate date or order for the Board. The date shown is the early end of the window; "early next year" falls in 2027. (~Dec 2026). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-07.

item.title: Expected · Pier 70 Parcel A: The Phase 1 down market delay, which tolls the… (Dec 26, 2026)
item.description: The Phase 1 down market delay, which tolls the developer's time-sensitive DDA obligations including close of escrow on option parcels, is extended to December 26, 2026: it reached its 60-month maximum in June 2026 and the parties agreed to extend it six months to allow time to complete the DDA amendments (Item 11A, memo of Aug 7, 2026, p.4: "the parties mutually agreed to extend the down market delay for an additional six months to December 26, 2026"). This is the end date of an extension the parties agreed under the DDA; the report does not call it a deadline, and it is not a forecast. (Dec 26, 2026). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-07.

item.title: Expected · Pier 70 Parcel A: Proposed DDA amendment: developer must close escrow on… (~2029)
item.description: Proposed DDA amendment: developer must close escrow on remaining Phase 1 parcels A, C2B and D by 2029-2030 or the Port will publicly offer them (~2029). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-07.

item.title: Expected · Pier 70 Parcel A: Parcel A is a Phase 1 parcel (Port Item 11A, Aug 2026, p.5)… (~2042)
item.description: Parcel A is a Phase 1 parcel (Port Item 11A, Aug 2026, p.5), and its own DDA outside dates are Phase 1 dates, tolled by the down market delay (extended to December 26, 2026); vertical construction on it remains paused. 2042 is not a deadline for this parcel: it is Pier & Point's arithmetic for the DDA's Phase 3 outside date (approximately 25 years after Project approval; the Port's report states no calendar year), shown only as the project's outermost bound (~2042). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2017-09-22; Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-07.
item.source: Port of San Francisco, 2017-09-22; Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-07

item.description: Phase 1 down market delay reaches its 60-month maximum; the parties extend it by six months to December 26, 2026 while DDA amendments are drafted (~Jun 2026). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-07.
